clue.text: Race boldly organised as contest between neighbours

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has arranged a bold race between two rival neighbourhoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges RACEBOLDLY. A LOCAL DERBY is a match between two teams from the same area, a common British sporting term.
explanation.definitionFit: A derby in British sport is a match between near rivals, and a local one pits neighbouring towns or clubs against each other.

clue.text: Bound to be left open for poets

parts.note: ope is an archaic, poetic form of the word open

explanation.surface: Something is obliged to be left open for the benefit of poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'obliged' but is the definition, in the sense of a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long bounding strides, so a bound is a near synonym.

clue.text: Company giving credit points

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
E (east) is a compass point
W (west) is another compass point

explanation.surface: A firm is handing out credit points, as on a loyalty scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or aircraft's company is its crew, the group of people working together.

clue.text: One has nobody up in the ring with right punch, say

definitions.text: One has nobody up in the ring

parts.note: a liberty is a right or freedom
the Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught horse, so a punch is an example of one

explanation.surface: A boxer with no opponent standing in the ring throws a right punch.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a circus ring, not a boxing ring: a LIBERTY HORSE performs there without a rider, so 'nobody up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus horses that perform loose, with no rider on their backs, are called by this name.

clue.text: Rotten school report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the school's name is taken as spoken

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school has issued a dreadful report card.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private (public) school.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood or fabric that is rotten has been eaten away, by worms or decay.

clue.text: Regularly tapped in lobby, one shows the pressure

definitions.text: Regularly tapped in lobby, one shows the pressure

parts.words: Regularly tapped in lobby, one shows the pressure
parts.note: a hall instrument people habitually tap on passing to see whether the weather reading has moved

explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures atmospheric pressure and traditionally hangs in a hallway where people tap its glass.

clue.text: Fell for composer dropping in

indicators.note: dropping says the word that follows is let fall from the composer's name

parts.note: Chopin was the Polish composer and pianist

explanation.surface: Someone fell for a composer who happened to drop in for a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like 'fell in love', but it is the verb meaning cut down; 'dropping in' takes IN out of CHOPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to chop it down.

clue.text: Parts nobody believes in

parts.note: regions of the world where no one holds the faith, read as places rather than roles nobody finds convincing

explanation.definitionFit: The whole realm of unbelievers, those outside a religion, is the territory meant.

clue.text: A few words in support of the standard interpretation

indicators.note: in a down clue, being in support of something means sitting beneath it, so these pieces come below

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a phrase is a short group of words

explanation.surface: Someone offers a few words backing the conventional reading of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the standard' is PAR; in a down entry, 'in support of' puts A PHRASE underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase restates a passage in other words, an interpretation of its meaning.

clue.text: Prayers best revised without a lot of elders

indicators.note: revised means altered or reworked, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: the a is the letter left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A prayer book's best prayers were revised, omitting quite a few, for the church elders.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of PRAYERS BEST, remove the A ('without a'), and rearrange the rest. 'lot of' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Presbyters were the elders of the early Christian church, and the term survives in Presbyterian church government.

clue.text: Just entertainment

definitions.meaning: a funfair or travelling show is a form of entertainment

explanation.definitionFit: Fair means equitable, and a fair is also a travelling show of rides and stalls.

clue.text: Helpful number

definitions.meaning: helpful in the sense of playing a useful part in bringing something about
a number is a piece of music, here one with no vocals

explanation.definitionFit: Being instrumental in something means helping it happen, and an instrumental is a musical piece without singing.

clue.text: British skater's skill needed in international meetings?

parts.note: a made-up word for the craft of a rinkman, someone at home on the skating rink

explanation.surface: A British ice skater's talent is required at international competitions.
explanation.walkthrough: RINKMANSHIP is coined on the pattern of seamanship. 'International meetings' turn out to be diplomatic summits, not skating championships.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing a dangerous situation to the edge of conflict to gain advantage is a diplomatic tactic used in tense summit talks.

clue.text: Cooking dinner, I get this part of it

indicators.note: cooking means preparing or tampering with, so the letters of the following words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone making dinner gets to handle one portion of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' rearranges DINNERIGET; the definition points back to the dinner, of which the answer is a component.
explanation.definitionFit: Each item that goes into a dish is a component of the whole meal.

clue.text: What gives Air force, say, direction and power?

definitions.text: What gives Air force, say, direction and power?

parts.words: What gives Air force, say, direction and power?
parts.note: air force is read as the force of the air, the wind, whose strength an instrument records

explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures wind speed and often its direction, telling the force of moving air.

clue.text: The kind of farm butter kids need

definitions.text: The kind of farm butter kids need

parts.words: The kind of farm butter kids need
parts.note: the butter is a farm animal that butts, and the kids are young goats needing their mother, read against the idea of children and dairy produce

explanation.definitionFit: A female goat butts with her head and is the mother whom young goats rely on.

clue.text: Haberdasher abroad better qualified?

parts.note: out means away from home, as abroad does
fitter means more fit, that is more suitable or better qualified

explanation.surface: A clothes shop owner overseas may be the better qualified one.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothing and accessories, as a haberdasher does.

clue.text: Singer's theme

definitions.meaning: a singer with a high male voice
the theme or general drift of a speech or text

explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a high male voice, and the tenor of an argument is its gist.

clue.text: Lover needing ring puts capital up front

indicators.note: up front says the capital city goes ahead of the ring in the answer

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a ring is round, so it is the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover who needs an engagement ring puts his money down in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money paid up front, but it is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero gave his name to any ardent male lover.

clue.text: Punishing run in meandering setting

indicators.note: in says the run's letter is placed inside the word for meandering

parts.note: tortuous means full of twists and turns
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gruelling run through a winding landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' is a link word. Do not confuse tortuous (winding) with the answer (causing torture).
explanation.definitionFit: Something punishing is agonising, like torture.

clue.text: So tamed etc, I'd reformed?

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so all the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tamed and so on admits they have mended their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the anagram fodder and also describes an animal brought under control.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that has been tamed and changed in its ways has been brought into the household.

clue.text: Turn aside right after welcome

indicators.note: after says the right comes behind the welcome in the answer

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting hail, a welcome

explanation.surface: Someone veers to the right just after being greeted.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to turn it away or ward it off.

clue.text: Size of type showing abnormal appetite

definitions.meaning: a printing size of twelve points
a medical craving to eat things that are not food, such as earth or chalk

explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a twelve-point typesetting size and also a disorder involving cravings for non-food substances.

clue.text: Refuse in secluded part of house an unknown quantity

parts.note: a den is a private retreat room in a house
in algebra, y stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Rubbish found in a quiet back room of a house, in amounts nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the noun rubbish but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a request is to turn it down.

clue.text: Common grub found in wheat-stalks

indicators.note: found in says the answer is sitting within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: An ordinary larva is discovered living in wheat stems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like an insect larva, but it is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, as is grub.

clue.text: One way sage is surviving in the city

parts.note: a street is one type of road or way
sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: A one-way system is the clever way of getting by in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the shrewd know-how to cope with urban life is being street-smart.

clue.text: Go for a walk round corner

definitions.meaning: a go is someone's chance in a game, as in my go
a short stroll, as in taking a quick spin outside

explanation.definitionFit: A turn is one's go in a game, a short stroll, and a bend or corner.

clue.text: Prepare garden inside convent for one type of butterfly

indicators.note: inside says the gardening word goes within the religious house

parts.note: a friary is a religious community's house, a convent of friars
to till is to prepare soil for planting

explanation.surface: Monks dig a garden within their convent for a particular butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritillaries are orange-brown butterflies with chequered wings.
